articles.title: Git Bash
articles.description: All things relating to the command line interface (CLI)
articles.contents:
Getting started
Git Bash comes with the git install. If you don’t have git installed, download it from the git site.
Set-up
By default it will assume the email linked to your laptop. If the email associated with your Github account is not your PSRC email, use the commands below to change it.
In the git bash terminal type the following but using your own Github username and email linked to Github:
git config --global user.name "myusername"
git config --global user.email myemail@gmail.com
To verify that the changes have been made:
git config --list
For video instructions on setting up your email and username in git, click on this short Youtube tutorial.
While pushing for the first time, the terminal will ask for username and password. If you have previously generated a personal token, the personal token should be used in lieu of your password.

articles.title: Git & Github Sessions
articles.description: 2026-27 Mini sessions on Branching, Pull Requests & Merges, and Undoing things
articles.contents:
Agenda
Session #1 (Nov 10, 2026): Branching
Why branch?
How to branch and know which branch you’re on by exploring different tools (Github Desktop, RStudio, Git Bash) to see what options you have
Session #2 (TBD): Pull Requests & Merges
Why and how to create a pull request (PR)
How to merge branches
Session #3 (TBD): Undoing
How to undo at each stage of the process:
Unstaged
Staged
Committed but not yet pushed to Github
Committed and already pushed Github

Restore a single-file from an old commit (but not the whole repo!)
Pre-work
Create a Github account
Download Github Desktop, RStudio, R, git (Git Bash comes with your git install)
Clone the repository git-together
Sign into your Github account
